links.note: Animals use lungs/gills, plants use stomata - 32767's respiration paragraph, the only one that names stomata.
Naming germination from the emergence of a shoot: section 10.2's opening definition, held by 32769.
Seed coat. The chapter mentions the seed's parts only inside section 10.2's germination treatment (water softens the coat so the embryo can develop), which is 32769; 32770 is only the light rule.
Stomata as the leaf pores for air exchange - 32767.
Reproduction defined as producing new ones of one's own kind - 32768's wording.
Drosera is named only in 32766, where insectivorous movement is used to show plants move without travelling.
Spawn is the egg stage of the frog cycle, which 32776 holds; 32774 is the mosquito.
Crescograph - 32772's Bose note.
Plants excreting excess water and minerals as droplets on leaves is stated in 32767's excretion paragraph.
Definition of stimulus - 32768.
Definition of excretion - 32767.
Breathing as air moving in and out, part of respiration - 32767's own sentence.
Water softening the seed coat is the mechanism behind pot A's failure in 32769's design.
Roots grow downwards - the Activity 10.3 result in 32771, not a germination condition.
Touch-me-not folding on touch is named in 32768 as a plant stimulus response.
What the tadpole's tail is for. The chapter states only that the tail disappears (32776); the advantage of having it is asked as an exercise, which is 32778.
Climbers winding around a nearby object is one of 32766's three plant movements.
Urine as an excretion product in animals - stated in 32767.
Bose showing plants sense and respond to stimuli - 32772. 32768 defines stimulus but names no scientist.
Seed turning into a sprout = germination, section 10.2's definition in 32769.
Light is the condition that is NOT universally essential - precisely 32770's distinction (coleus and petunia need it, other seeds do not). 32769 would be the water/air pair.
Stagnant water as the mosquito's breeding stages: 32774 carries the safety audit for stagnant water and the four stages it shelters.
The car-versus-yourself comparison is 32765's worked example; movement alone separates nothing.
Drosera's sticky-ended hairs and insect nutrition are described in 32766.
Respiration as an essential characteristic - 32767, which introduces breathing and respiration on the reader's own body.
Excretion in plants (droplets on grasses and roses) is 32767's closing example.
Stimulus defined plus the thorn and touch-me-not examples - both from 32768.
The answer is the conditional three-part rule (water, air, suitable light and/or dark), which 32770 states and explains; 32769 only establishes water and air.
Water's role in germination - pot A of 32769's design and its stated reason.
Air in the spaces between soil particles - the reason 32769 gives for the flooded pot failing.
Root down, shoot up and towards sunlight - the three-beaker conclusion in 32771.
Tadpole-to-froglet transition is in 32776's frog sequence; 32774 is the mosquito's four stages.
Froglet against adult frog in habitat and body - 32776's point that the changes show in shape, structure and habitat.
The seed coat's role during germination - section 10.2 content, carried by 32769.
Death defined as failing to exhibit the characteristics despite food, air and water - the closing paragraph of 32768.
Soil air spaces serving both germination and root expansion - the air condition of 32769.
Plants moving without travelling, with flower opening, Drosera and climbers as examples - 32766 in full.
